chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce is that he says to her, Begin your waiting period (iddah), or he says to her, You are divorced.

key_terms.اعْتَدِّي: Command form of i'tadda — begin your waiting period (iddah); a valid divorce formula in Shia fiqh
key_terms.الطَّلَاق: Talaq — divorce; the dissolution of the marriage contract by the husband verbal declaration
key_terms.طَالِق: Adjective meaning divorced/free; the direct declaration formula for divorce

ai.seo_question: What are the valid verbal formulas for divorce (talaq) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the valid verbal formula for divorce (talaq) in Islamic law, specifying two acceptable phrases: commanding the wife to begin her iddah (waiting period) or directly declaring her divorced. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence because it restricts divorce to explicit, unambiguous formulations, excluding implicit or euphemistic expressions. The Imam addressed jurists and students of fiqh, who understood these formulations within the broader Quranic framework of divorce regulations in Surat al-Talaq.
